verses.1: In those days, as the number of disciples was increasing, there arose a complaint from the Greek-speaking Jews against the Hebrews. It was because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution.
verses.2: So the Twelve called together the whole body of disciples and said, "It is not right for us to neglect the word of God in order to serve tables.
verses.3: Look among you, brothers, for seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and wisdom, and we will appoint them over this matter.
verses.4: But we ourselves will remain in prayer and in the work of the word."
verses.5: The proposal pleased the whole group, and they selected Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicolaus, a proselyte from Antioch.
verses.6: These they brought before the apostles, and after prayer, they laid hands on them.
verses.7: Then the word of God continued to grow, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem greatly increased, and a great company of the priests became obedient to the faith.
verses.8: Stephen, full of grace and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people.
verses.9: But some from the synagogue called the Libertines, and from Cyrenes, Alexandrians, and from those from Cilicia and Asia, began to argue with Stephen,
verses.10: and they were not able to resist the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
verses.11: Then they brought forward men who said, "We have heard him speaking blasphemous words about Moses and God.
verses.12: They stirred up the people, along with the elders and the scribes, and they rushed upon him and seized him, bringing him before the council.
verses.13: They also brought forward false witnesses, who said, "This man does not stop speaking words against the holy place and the law.
verses.14: For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs that Moses handed down to us."
verses.15: And all the members of the council looked intently at Stephen, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "παρεθεωροῦντο" is rendered as "were being neglected" to capture the passive voice and the sense of oversight.
- v. 3: "μαρτυρουμένους" is "men of good reputation" to emphasize their character.
- v. 5: "προσήλυτον Ἀντιοχέα" is "a proselyte from Antioch" to preserve the geographic reference and status.
- v. 14: "τὸν τόπον τοῦ ἁγίου" is translated as "the holy place" to retain the reference to the temple.
raw:
[1] In those days, as the number of disciples was increasing, there arose a complaint from the Greek-speaking Jews against the Hebrews. It was because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution.
[2] So the Twelve called together the whole body of disciples and said, "It is not right for us to neglect the word of God in order to serve tables.
[3] Look among you, brothers, for seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and wisdom, and we will appoint them over this matter.
[4] But we ourselves will remain in prayer and in the work of the word."
[5] The proposal pleased the whole group, and they selected Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicolaus, a proselyte from Antioch.
[6] These they brought before the apostles, and after prayer, they laid hands on them.
[7] Then the word of God continued to grow, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem greatly increased, and a great company of the priests became obedient to the faith.
[8] Stephen, full of grace and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people.
[9] But some from the synagogue called the Libertines, and from Cyrenes, Alexandrians, and from those from Cilicia and Asia, began to argue with Stephen,
[10] and they were not able to resist the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
[11] Then they brought forward men who said, "We have heard him speaking blasphemous words about Moses and God.
[12] They stirred up the people, along with the elders and the scribes, and they rushed upon him and seized him, bringing him before the council.
[13] They also brought forward false witnesses, who said, "This man does not stop speaking words against the holy place and the law.
[14] For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs that Moses handed down to us."
[15] And all the members of the council looked intently at Stephen, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.

---
Notes
- v. 1: "παρεθεωροῦντο" is rendered as "were being neglected" to capture the passive voice and the sense of oversight.
- v. 3: "μαρτυρουμένους" is "men of good reputation" to emphasize their character.
- v. 5: "προσήλυτον Ἀντιοχέα" is "a proselyte from Antioch" to preserve the geographic reference and status.
- v. 14: "τὸν τόπον τοῦ ἁγίου" is translated as "the holy place" to retain the reference to the temple.
